title: Program Kit alpha version transition
intent: Establish explicit version intents, replace pre-stable Program Kit-owned contract revisions with alpha ordinals, and coordinate every packaged first-party deliverable at 0.1.0-alpha.2 without rewriting external selections or immutable history.
scope: A closed repository inventory that classifies product release versions, owned artifact revisions, external selections, historical evidence revisions, and fixture revisions.
A replaceable alpha progression policy that validates explicit human-selected next versions without choosing release authority.
Alpha replacement revisions and deterministic migrations for every active Program Kit-owned schema, contract, policy, capability, plan, design, and comparable governed identity.
Architecture Design 0.1.0-alpha.2, Implementation Plan 0.1.0-alpha.3, and StaticConformanceDisposition 0.1.0-alpha.1 as the first transitioned design-flow contracts.
One exact 0.1.0-alpha.2 product release identity across NuGet packages, CLI metadata, capability bundle content, and generated first-party package references.
An independent capability-bundle manifest-format revision, byte-exact bundle regeneration, thin provider-wrapper verification, and isolated initialization proof.
A second-stage review set under the transitioned contracts for refresh, contributor setup, Console reachability, public analyzers, and the eventual JTest migration prompt.
nonGoals: Defining or enforcing stable patch, minor, or major compatibility progression before Release Kit is designed.
Publishing, promoting, deploying, or releasing 0.1.0-alpha.2 to a package feed.
Rewriting immutable historical approvals, closure evidence, receipts, third-party versions, SDK versions, target frameworks, or intentional fixtures.
Implementing capability refresh behavior, the .contributors maintainer setup, Console generation reachability, or public analyzer behavior in this transition.
Mutating JTest or any other consumer repository.
Activating Program Kit source capabilities in the Program Kit authoring workspace.
Creating hooks, watchers, autonomous agents, provider-global configuration, or runtime application architecture.
assumptions: The existing exact version-map and migration-assessment mechanisms remain suitable foundations once version intent and alpha progression are explicit.
Legacy stable-looking contract revisions remain readable and immutable while active selectors move through registered migrations.
The current private Program Kit C# gate remains compatible with Program Kit-owned transition implementation.
Release Kit will own the later stable progression strategy and the explicit transition to 1.0.0.
The Program Kit repository can prove capability initialization in an isolated consumer workspace without activating those capabilities at its authoring root.

The current implemented central NuGet package version baseline before the coordinated alpha.2 change.
The current bundleVersion and kitVersion split, exact capability bytes, provider adapters, and supporting resources that must migrate without activation.
The current exact-node and typed-dependency version-map behavior.
The current reverse dependency closure, exact selection, explicit decision, and fail-closed migration assessment behavior.
The current human authority boundary, current Architecture and Planning contract requirements, static-conformance procedure, and stop-before-implementation rule.

domains.purpose: Own version-intent classification, immutable identity revisions, alpha progression validation, compatibility recording, and migration closure.

vocabulary.meaning: The declared semantic role of a version value: product release, owned artifact revision, external selection, historical evidence revision, or fixture revision.
The one-based revision counter in 0.1.0-alpha.N for one stable Program Kit-owned governed identity during the pre-stable policy.
A replaceable contract that validates an explicit proposed next version against identity history and never supplies release authority.

domains.purpose: Own one coordinated product release identity across every packaged first-party Program Kit deliverable and embedded current first-party dependency selection.

vocabulary.meaning: The exact coordinated Program Kit version shared by NuGet packages, CLI metadata, capability bundle content, and generated current first-party package references.
The independently versioned owned contract that defines the capability-bundle manifest shape; it is not the bundle content release.

domains.purpose: Own inert canonical capability packaging, thin provider wrappers, exact bundle bytes, isolated initialization, and authoring-workspace denial.

vocabulary.meaning: A canonical provider-neutral capability definition authored in Program Kit and never activated from the Program Kit authoring root.
A consumer-workspace provider wrapper bound by an ownership lock to exact canonical capability bytes in an explicitly selected Program Kit root.

semanticModels.meaning: A closed classification of every active version-bearing repository value before any automated progression or rewrite.
semanticModels.invariants: Every active value has exactly one intent; product and owned-artifact clocks are never conflated; external, evidence, and fixture values cannot become product or public-contract releases through defaulting.

semanticModels.meaning: A stable governed identity with immutable revisions whose pre-stable versions progress as 0.1.0-alpha.N.
semanticModels.invariants: New identities begin at alpha.1; changed canonical bytes advance exactly one ordinal; identity plus version plus digest is immutable; compatibility and migration disposition are explicit; no stable SemVer significance is inferred.

semanticModels.meaning: One human-selected Program Kit release value projected into every first-party packaged surface.
semanticModels.invariants: The central selected value is 0.1.0-alpha.2 for this transition; package artifacts and current generated references agree exactly; bundle format remains an independent owned contract; publication remains separately authorized.

semanticModels.meaning: An explicit mapping from each active stable-looking legacy revision to one immutable alpha replacement revision.
semanticModels.invariants: Legacy bytes and evidence are not rewritten; replacement identities remain stable; selectors move only through registered migrations; reverse dependency closure and incompatible or undecided edges fail closed.

referenceRules.referencingScope: Program Kit-owned schema, contract, policy, capability, plan, design, disposition, and comparable governed artifact revisions
referenceRules.referencedScope: The coordinated Program Kit product release value as an inferred owned-artifact revision
referenceRules.rationale: Product release and owned-artifact revision are independent clocks; a coincidental number never establishes compatibility.

referenceRules.referencingScope: First-party Program Kit package metadata, CLI release metadata, capability bundle content metadata, and generated current first-party package references
referenceRules.referencedScope: One explicit central product release selection
referenceRules.rationale: One finite source eliminates release drift and permits exact package and generated-output verification.

referenceRules.referencingScope: Alpha version transition rewrites and active-selector migration
referenceRules.referencedScope: External selections, immutable historical approval or closure evidence, receipts, and explicit fixture identities as values to renumber
referenceRules.rationale: Those values carry upstream, evidentiary, or synthetic meaning and are not current Program Kit product or owned-contract releases.

artifactDecisions.requestedOutcome: Represent the exact pre-stable version-intent, contract migration, coordinated package baseline, capability transition, and follow-on design boundary as one canonical reviewed design.

executableBehavior.rationale: The design records architecture and grants no implementation, package publication, capability activation, or consumer mutation authority.

valueLifecycle.rationale: The design is schema-validated, compared with source truth, and digest-bound by a separate implementation plan and review manifest.

agentRetrieval.rationale: The review artifacts are addressed through explicit repository paths.

agentProcedure.rationale: This artifact creates no capability, wrapper, hook, watcher, or autonomous procedure.

humanCommunication.audience: The human Program Kit architecture reviewer, future maintainers, and implementation contributors.
humanCommunication.decisionAuthorityBoundary: Only explicit human approval of the exact canonical design and implementation-plan digests authorizes implementation; release and publication remain separate decisions.
humanCommunication.rationale: The transition changes public contract selection, package identity, capability packaging, and future contributor expectations.

generatedNavigation.rationale: The bounded review directory provides explicit navigation without a generated index.

governance.provenancePolicy: The exact human intent and repository evidence are named; generated projections and future implementation observations do not retroactively become architecture authority.
governance.digestPolicy: The review manifest binds exact design and plan bytes; any change requires revalidation, new digests, and a new human decision.
governance.compatibilityPolicy: Changing version-intent categories, alpha ordinal progression, the coordinated product-release boundary, migration failure semantics, capability authority, or stable-policy ownership requires a new reviewed design revision.
governance.migrationPolicy: This transitional design remains on Architecture Design 2.0.0 only to establish the replacement alpha contract set; the follow-on health design must use Architecture Design 0.1.0-alpha.2.

dataHandling.redactionPolicy: The design contains no secrets, credentials, tokens, consumer data, or machine-specific user paths.
dataHandling.externalizationPolicy: Only committed review artifacts and exact digests may be shared.
dataHandling.ephemeralDataPolicy: Build outputs, temporary workspaces, package archives, runtime state, and local initialization roots remain outside the canonical design.

artifactDecisions.rationale: A canonical current-format design is required to cross the contract-version boundary without assuming authority from the not-yet-established alpha contracts.

security.policy: Version processing reads only explicit repository inputs and performs no feed, provider, secret, or network discovery.
guarantees: Exact paths, versions, and digests are validated before migration or projection.
Generated and initialized outputs remain subject to path-containment and ownership checks.
exclusions: Package-feed credentials, signing, promotion, deployment, and provider trust are outside this transition.

authority.policy: Humans select product releases, approve exact designs and plans, decide compatibility, and authorize migration; tooling only validates and projects explicit selections.
guarantees: No version is bumped, package published, capability activated, or consumer migrated autonomously.
The current review stops before implementation and the follow-on review stops again before its implementation.
exclusions: Approval of recommendations is not treated as approval of later canonical design or plan bytes.

secrets.policy: No transition contract, migration, package build, bundle check, or isolated initialization needs a secret.
guarantees: Verification is local and operates on repository or generated fixture bytes.
exclusions: Feed authentication, signing keys, provider credentials, and consumer secrets are not read or recorded.

persistence.policy: Canonical revisions, migration definitions, registries, and review artifacts are immutable digest-bound repository files; projections are regenerated.
guarantees: Legacy revisions and historical evidence remain byte-unchanged.
New alpha revisions use new exact paths or registrations and atomic generated-output publication where applicable.
exclusions: No database, remote registry, package feed, user-global state, or consumer repository is an authority.

failure.policy: Ambiguous intent, duplicate identity-version pairs, digest drift, skipped alpha ordinals, unresolved migrations, version disagreement, or unsafe output fails closed with deterministic diagnostics.
guarantees: Validation reports every classified path and every incompatible or undecided dependency edge.
Partial package, schema, bundle, or capability transitions cannot be accepted as closure.
exclusions: Tooling never guesses intent, compatibility, migration authority, or the stable version strategy.

concurrency.policy: Inventory, generation, and validation may parallelize only over immutable inputs; final registry, package, and bundle promotion is serialized.
guarantees: Concurrent validation cannot change selections or canonical bytes.
One final exact inventory and release selection governs closure.
exclusions: No watcher or autonomous refresh loop is introduced.

cancellation.policy: Cancellation stops before promotion or leaves the previous complete canonical or generated state intact.
guarantees: Temporary outputs are outside authoritative roots until verification succeeds.
Cancellation never implies approval, rollback of committed history, or silent retry.
exclusions: External package publication and consumer migration are not started.

observability.policy: Deterministic reports expose classification, old and new exact revisions, digests, migration decisions, package agreement, bundle verification, initialization isolation, tests, and changed paths.
guarantees: Review and closure evidence distinguishes implemented, scaffolded, deferred, historical, and external claims.
Every artifact in the review set is digest-bound.
exclusions: Telemetry, remote evidence transport, and consumer data capture are not introduced.

compatibility.policy: Version intents evolve independently; active contract replacement requires explicit compatibility and migration disposition even though stable patch/minor/major enforcement is deferred.
guarantees: Identity plus version plus digest denotes one immutable revision.
Legacy-to-alpha mappings are explicit and reverse dependency closure is assessed.
First-party packaged outputs agree exactly on 0.1.0-alpha.2.
exclusions: Matching numbers do not imply compatibility and external selections are never renumbered.

scenarios.intent: Classify every active version-bearing repository source before changing any version.
preconditions: The repository source and active artifact registries are available at one exact commit.
steps: Enumerate finite version-bearing sources and their exact paths and digests.
Assign exactly one version intent, owner, active status, and transition disposition to each source.
Reject duplicates, missing classifications, and inferred category changes.
Review the complete inventory before any rewrite or selector migration.
outcomes: Every active value is explicitly classified.
External selections, immutable history, and fixtures are protected from product or contract renumbering.
failureOutcomes: An unclassified or ambiguously classified value blocks the transition.

scenarios.intent: Replace active stable-looking Program Kit-owned revisions with immutable alpha ordinal revisions.
preconditions: The complete inventory and replaceable alpha progression policy conform.
The exact source and target identities, digests, compatibility decisions, and migration authority are explicit.
steps: Materialize new alpha schema, contract, policy, capability, plan, design, and disposition revisions without changing legacy bytes.
Register exact old-to-new migration definitions and update internal exact references.
Run schema, semantic, version-map, migration-assessment, and historical-immutability conformance.
Move active selectors only after the dependency closure is fully decided.
outcomes: Architecture Design selects 0.1.0-alpha.2, Implementation Plan selects 0.1.0-alpha.3, and StaticConformanceDisposition selects 0.1.0-alpha.1.
All other active owned identities use the correct independent alpha ordinal.
Legacy revisions remain available as immutable migration sources.
failureOutcomes: Skipped ordinals, changed legacy bytes, duplicate exact keys, stale references, or unresolved migration edges prevent selector movement.

scenarios.intent: Prepare every first-party packaged Program Kit deliverable at 0.1.0-alpha.2.
preconditions: The human-selected product release is exactly 0.1.0-alpha.2.
The package projection target inventory is finite and reviewed.
steps: Project the exact release into central package metadata, CLI metadata, bundle content metadata, and current generated first-party package references.
Assign the capability-bundle manifest format its independent alpha contract revision.
Build and inspect all packages and the exact capability bundle without publishing.
Generate representative hosts and verify that every current first-party package reference is 0.1.0-alpha.2.
outcomes: No packaged first-party component has version drift.
Bundle content release and bundle manifest format are distinguishable.
Local package and generated-host conformance passes.
failureOutcomes: Any missing target, conflicting literal, stale bundle digest, or package mismatch blocks closure.

scenarios.intent: Move design procedures to alpha contracts without activating Program Kit source capabilities.
preconditions: The new design, planning, and static-conformance contracts and migrations pass.
The existing human authority and stop boundaries remain unchanged.
steps: Update canonical design and gate-design procedures to the exact alpha contract versions.
Keep provider adapters thin and regenerate the capability bundle with exact source and output digests.
Initialize an isolated consumer fixture from the explicit Program Kit root and verify ownership-lock refresh.
Reject initialization when the selected workspace is the Program Kit authoring root.
outcomes: A future design session can produce Architecture Design alpha.2, Implementation Plan alpha.3, and StaticConformanceDisposition alpha.1 artifacts.
The source capabilities remain inert in the authoring workspace.
failureOutcomes: Copied semantics in a wrapper, stale bundle bytes, unsafe overwrite, manual-fix dependency, or authoring-root activation blocks closure.

scenarios.intent: Produce the remaining health design under the transitioned alpha contracts.
preconditions: The transition implementation is complete and its exact alpha contracts are active.
The human has started the follow-on design work.
steps: Design deterministic installed-bundle refresh and re-initialization.
Design the .contributors maintainer-workspace setup at the parent of the checkout.
Design Console CLI and refresh reachability with exact compilation inputs.
Design opt-in public analyzers without exposing private PKCS policy.
Produce and validate the separate alpha-contract review set and stop for exact human approval.
outcomes: All deferred health concerns are represented by bounded dependency-ordered work units.
The eventual JTest migration prompt is derived only after Program Kit implementation and verification complete.
failureOutcomes: The follow-on design cannot begin under legacy design-flow contracts or silently implement behavior.

statusClaims.claim: The current-format transitional design exists for validation and exact human review; it does not claim approval or implementation.
The replaceable alpha progression validator is prospective and has not been implemented.
The coordinated 0.1.0-alpha.2 projection and verification are prospective; current package and bundle drift remains implemented source truth.
